clue.text: Leader dropped from modest expedition

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for modest is dropped off the front

parts.note: chaste means modest, pure

explanation.surface: Someone's modest journey has lost its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' here is not a journey but its older sense of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its older sense is promptness or speed, the same as hurry.

clue.text: Footballer over 27 is not spoken of

indicators.note: in a down answer the footballer piece is placed over, so above, the other piece

parts.note: a half (halfback) is a footballing position
the answer to 27 across means bar, an obstacle; a hitch is a snag

explanation.surface: A footballer past 27 is never mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not spoken of' is a sound pun: a knot, spoken of. 27 is HINDRANCE, for which HITCH is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple sailor's knot, said aloud as a 'not'.

clue.text: Dwarf in dangerous trick

definitions.meaning: to dwarf here is to check growth, to keep small
a risky feat performed for show

explanation.surface: A small person takes part in a risky trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To check growth, and a daredevil feat.

clue.text: Decoration on shoulder and bottom of costume on girl

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Trim on the shoulder and hem of a girl's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental strap worn on the shoulder of a uniform.

clue.text: Hunt after short cuts supported by runners

indicators.note: the hunt piece comes after the short cuts piece in the answer

parts.note: bobs are short haircuts
Leigh Hunt was an English poet and essayist, so Hunt points to his first name

explanation.surface: A hunt follows a few quick shortcuts, the riders carried on runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' wants to be a chase; it is the surname of the poet Leigh Hunt, whose first name is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing sled rides down an ice track on steel runners.

clue.text: Swimmer cured using money put in the hat

indicators.note: the money letter is put inside the hat word

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat
L stands for pounds, as in the £ sign from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A fish restored to health by cash dropped in the hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' looks like healed; it means smoked and salted.
explanation.definitionFit: A herring salted and smoked whole.

clue.text: Bit of the sea I tried at first to run through

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word tried is used

explanation.surface: Someone first tries running through a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run through' is to stab with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab with the blade fixed to a rifle.

clue.text: When talking, Scandinavians turn away

indicators.note: spoken aloud the word for these Scandinavians gives a sound-alike

parts.note: Lapps are the people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Northern Europeans turn away mid-conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapps is an older name for the Sami people of Lapland.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall away from a standard or faith.

clue.text: Society changed its tune about it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, so around, the word it
the letters of its tune are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A society reworks its song around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society' looks like the clue's subject; it is the definition, a learned body. The second 'it' is both the inserted word and the surface's object.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation for a learned or professional purpose.

clue.text: With orders to admit the press

indicators.note: the words with orders let in, and so contain, the run of letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to let in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the press' looks like journalists; it means a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a throng or crowd, as is a large mob.

clue.text: Eulogistic archbishop accompanying a politician

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A eulogy delivered by an archbishop with a politician at his side.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech full of praise for someone.

clue.text: Question about a bribe that's been returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a sop is something given to pacify or buy off, a bribe

explanation.surface: A query about a bribe that was handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been returned' turns RESOP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A baffling problem or puzzle is a hard question.

clue.text: Much favoured, the Spanish holiday accommodation

parts.note: a hot favourite is one much favoured, as in the betting
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A popular Spanish holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers stay in such a building with rooms to let.

clue.text: Characters from Argentine or from Morocco

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are used as raw characters and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is either Argentine or Moroccan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Morocco' looks like a nationality; it means a native of Tangier, the Moroccan port.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tangier, the Moroccan port city, is so called.

clue.text: Barman, one who tries to go around quietly

indicators.note: the word for one who tries is placed around the quiet letter

parts.note: a taster is one who tries food or drink
p (piano) is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: A barman who tries to slip around unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who draws beer from a tap serves in a pub.

clue.text: Fruit being about .03937" in length

indicators.note: the being word goes about, so around, the length piece

parts.note: a person is a being
.03937 of an inch is one millimetre: I (one) and MM

explanation.surface: A tiny fruit, barely a millimetre long.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is 25.4 millimetres, so .03937 inch is one millimetre.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange tropical fruit, like a tomato in shape.

clue.text: Run down advertising during break in the action

indicators.note: the advertising piece sits during, so within, the break piece

parts.note: a truce is a pause in the fighting
ad is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Adverts during a pause in play are criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' looks like slowing to a stop, but it means to disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or disparage someone is to speak ill of them.

clue.text: So topical a conversion of the pope

indicators.note: a conversion changes one thing into another, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A topical change of faith concerning the pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the pope as successor to Saint Peter the apostle.

clue.text: Key line in dialling system cut off

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: the line goes in the dialling system letters

parts.note: STD is subscriber trunk dialling, the old UK long-distance phone system
a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: A key phone line is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienated, separated from someone.

clue.text: It's very difficult when threads get broken

indicators.note: broken threads are tangled, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sewing is at its worst when the threads snap.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of tough means most difficult, here put as very difficult.

clue.text: Do trend to move underfoot

indicators.note: the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Follow the fashion and walk all over things.
explanation.definitionFit: Walked on, pressed down by feet.

clue.text: 26-0. — fast and furious

parts.note: read as a six-nil score: six is VI in Roman numerals and nought is the letter O
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A thrashing scoreline, with play fast and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed score is odd: 6-0 read as Roman VI and nought as O gives VIO, and the 2 seems a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging and fierce, full of force.

clue.text: See an animal make tracks

parts.note: v. is short for Latin vide, see
an is the indefinite article, a
a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: Look at an animal running off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make tracks' looks like footprints left by the animal; it means leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for leave in a hurry, clear off.

clue.text: Pantry not full yet?

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still to come'
if a place is not full there is room

explanation.surface: A larder with space left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeroom in a large house where preserves and drinks were kept.

clue.text: Slim girl finishes elevenses, may well skip lunch

indicators.note: the finishes are the last letters of the following five words

explanation.surface: A slender girl finishes her mid-morning snack and may skip lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender, graceful woman, after the airy spirit.

clue.text: It's put inside a ship

definitions.meaning: a lining or insert fitted inside something

explanation.surface: Something placed inside a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable lining, and an ocean-going passenger vessel.

clue.text: Transport to an Indian island

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in India

explanation.surface: Getting a ride to an island off India.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both an Indian horse cart and a Polynesian kingdom.

clue.text: Dives to catch ball in the air after line-out

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: the line letter is taken out

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in the air

explanation.surface: A player dives to catch the ball after a line-out in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus; 'line-out' looks like the rugby restart.
explanation.definitionFit: A very wealthy man, like the rich man of the parable.

clue.text: The sole answer?

parts.note: read as a fish: the sole is a flatfish whose common kinds include one named after a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The only solution there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only'; it is the flatfish, and the answer completes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common flatfish is named after this sour fruit.

clue.text: Defect after drawing a weapon

indicators.note: the defect piece comes after the drawing piece

parts.note: a doodle is an idle drawing
a bug is a defect, as in software

explanation.surface: Someone defects after drawing a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defect' looks like a verb, desert, and 'drawing a weapon' like unsheathing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The German V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War had this nickname.

clue.text: Rustic managed this foreign bar

parts.note: a hind is a farm labourer, a rustic
ran means managed, as a business
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A country fellow ran this bar abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it means an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle or impediment bars the way.

clue.text: Junior and senior pressmen jointly raised to power

parts.note: a cub reporter is a junior pressman
ed is short for editor, the senior person on a newspaper

explanation.surface: Junior and senior journalists together lifted to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised to power' is mathematical: multiplied by itself twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A number to the third power has been multiplied by itself twice.
